rationale: hammernik_2017-claude-agentic: vn_T=5, vn_n_filters=16, vn_kernel=9, vn_n_bumps=31, vn_x_range=2.0, vn_filter_init_std=0.05, vn_rbf_init_std=0.01, vn_lambda_init=0.02, epochs=20, batch_size=2, lr=0.0005, grad_clip=1.0, train_n=400, val_n=200, seed=42, max_train_s=1500, rationale=iter-8 (six-box; RE-DISPATCH cheaper after TIMEOUT). First attempt (T=5,f=16,ep=24,lr=5e-4,max_train_s=1680) was KILLED at the 30-min wall (elapsed 30:24, no obs) -- iter-6's identical-compute config ran 1732s, dangerously close to the 1800s kill, and iter-8 crossed it on a slower node before the epoch guard tripped. FINDING: T=5/ep=24 is not reproducibly budget-safe. FIX: keep the lr hypothesis, cut epochs 24->20 (DEPENDENT budget var, ~+200s margin) and tighten max_train_s 1680->1500 so the epoch loop breaks well before the kill. WIDTH axis falsified (iter-7 f=24 regressed); best=iter-6 (T=5,f=16,lambda=0.02, hr=0.6329). ONE KNOB vs iter-6: lr 9.6e-4 -> 5e-4 (~2x lower). HYPOTHESIS: a gentler lr lets the T=5 unroll settle into a lower-loss basin, hr > 0.6329; if it regresses, 9.6e-4 was already well-tuned. All else = iter-6 (T=5, f=16, kernel=9, n_bumps=31, x_range=2.0, lambda=0.02, batch=2, grad_clip=1.0, seed=42, train_n=400). VN plateaus early so ep=20 still converges. batch_size=2 (OOM guard); expandable_segments via --export.
